tasks.short: Scout rows for pests, disease and weeds, report them, look up allowed treatments, apply the grower's chosen product and record the use.

steps.what: Farmworker walks the rows and identifies plants, pests and weeds
Farmworker writes findings with row numbers: on a paper sheet today, in the crop registration app with a photo after the change
Farmworker checks the scouting report: rows, pests and weeds as seen, and photos that show them
Farmworker sends the checked scouting report to the grower
Farmworker looks up possible pesticides and fertilizers in the binder or the adviser's messages
Grower decides product, dose and timing with the crop adviser
Licensed farmworker mixes and applies the product
Farmworker records the actual product, dose, time and plot of the application: on paper for the grower to enter today, in the app after the change

tasks.design: The worker writes findings into the crop registration app ({OTHER}) on the phone with row, photo and pest from a list, checks them and sends them to the grower; the app's product database shows which products are authorised for that crop and pest. After the grower decides, the worker logs the application in the same app, which checks authorisation and dose at entry and keeps the electronic record the law now requires.
tasks.previous_blocker: Scouting notes and spray records were on paper and typed in later by the grower.
tasks.enabler_now: Crop registration apps log spraying in the field and warn on unauthorised products or doses; electronic records are becoming mandatory.
tasks.still_hard: Identifying pests is a trained eye; product choice stays with the grower and adviser.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting the first aphids on a few plants before they spread.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; records are made once, in the field.

reach.learn: Whether photo findings with locations sharpen advice.

evidence.claim: A crop registration app logs spraying on a phone in the field and warns on unauthorised products or exceeded doses.
Users must record product, time, dose, area and crop, and transfer non-electronic records to machine-readable form within 30 days for uses from 1 January 2026.
A Dutch draft makes incorrect or incomplete spray records fineable from 1 January 2027.
Logging work per glasshouse worker can monitor performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from scouting to the spray record; buying products is outside.
Input contract: plot and crop list kept by the grower in the app; authorised product database supplied by the app; fallback is paper and later entry.
Records are per plot, not per worker.
Grower and adviser time is outside the worker's savings.

Writing findings and the spray record are first records and keep their full time; the grower no longer types them in, which is outside the worker's savings. s3 keeps 50 because the product database replaces the binder but the worker still reads the options.
unknowns: Whether the farm already uses a crop registration app.
How often scouting happens per week.
research_questions: Do photo findings shorten the time from finding to treatment?

incremental.description: Grower keeps plots and crops current in the app.
No ongoing focal upkeep: the grower keeps plots and crops, and learning the app is a one-off.

approvals.approved_version: Product, dose, timing and plot as decided by the grower in s4; a change needs a new decision.
The scouting report with rows, findings and photos exactly as checked by the worker in s2c, sent once to the grower in the crop registration app; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the product database lacks many minor crops, so the worker still looks up most options (2.2); high: the database covers the farm's crops (5.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take orders, pick and load plants, write delivery notes, deliver to customers and take payment or signature.

steps.what: Farmworker takes plant orders: all by phone today; after the change only from customers who still phone
Regular customers order through the web shop
Farmworker picks and loads the plants and flowers
Farmworker writes the delivery note by hand
Farmworker drives and delivers to customers
Farmworker collects payment or proof of delivery: on paper today; after the change corrects delivered quantities on the phone and collects payment where due
Customer signs for the delivery on the driver's phone
Farmworker checks the signed delivery before the invoice is made: plants and quantities as actually delivered, and the customer's name
The checked delivery creates the invoice to the customer in the web shop

tasks.design: Regular customers order through a simple web shop on the {ECOMMERCE} platform with the nursery's stock and prices, so phone orders shrink. Delivery notes print from the order; at delivery the worker corrects the quantities actually delivered, the customer signs on the driver's phone, and after the worker's check the invoice is made; picking, loading and driving stay manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Orders came by phone and notes and invoices were written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Small web shops and delivery-signature apps are cheap and standard.
tasks.still_hard: Plant quality and availability change daily; regular customers like to call.
tasks.human_edge: Picking the best plants for a good customer and placing them well at the shop.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; less paperwork per delivery.

reach.learn: Whether a web shop with live stock replaces calls.

evidence.claim: Small web shops and delivery-signature apps are standard for small businesses.
Businesses must keep their administration and invoices under national tax rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from order to proof of delivery; invoicing follow-up is outside.
Input contract: stock and prices kept by the grower in the web shop; customer accounts set up by the grower; fallback is phone and paper.
Customer and grower time, including web orders (s1w) and signing (s5k), share 1 each, is outside the worker's savings.

Picking, loading, driving and the delivery check keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 for customers who still phone. s3 keeps 30 for checking the printed note. s5 keeps 60 for quantity changes and payments.
unknowns: Share of customers who would order online.
research_questions: Do online orders reduce picking errors?

incremental.description: Farmworker checks web orders against what is in stock.
Grower keeps stock and prices current in the web shop.

approvals.approved_version: The delivery with plants and quantities as actually delivered and the customer's signature, exactly as checked by the worker in s5c, invoiced once to that customer's account in the web shop; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most customers keep phoning and many pay on delivery (10.5); high: regular customers order online and sign on the phone (17.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Feel and look at leaves during crop work, check suspect leaves with a lens, mark the spot and tell the grower.

steps.what: Farmworker feels leaves and notes their coloring during crop work
Farmworker checks suspect leaves with a hand lens for insects or disease
Farmworker marks the spot with tape
Farmworker reports what was found: by walking to find the grower today; by logging it with a photo and row in the app after the change
Farmworker checks the finding before it goes: row, symptom and a photo that shows it
Farmworker sends the checked finding to the grower

tasks.design: Instead of walking off to find the grower, the worker logs the finding with photo and row in the crop registration app ({OTHER}), checks it and sends it to the grower. Feeling, looking and marking stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Findings were passed on by word of mouth.
tasks.enabler_now: Glasshouse registration apps register observations at the plant.
tasks.still_hard: Detection is touch and sight; nothing replaces the worker's attention in the row.
tasks.human_edge: Feeling a sticky leaf and knowing it means trouble.

reach.task: Decide on treatment after a finding
reach.learn: Whether photo reports speed the decision.

evidence.claim: A glasshouse app registers plants and clusters directly in the glasshouse.
Logging per worker can monitor performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from noticing a symptom to the grower informed; treatment is outside.
Input contract: row and plot numbers set up in the app by the grower; fallback is telling the grower in person.
Findings are logged per row, not to judge workers.
Inspection by touch and sight, marking, checking and sending keep their full time. s4 keeps 60: the walk to find the grower goes, but writing the finding takes time.
unknowns: Whether workers carry phones in the glasshouse.
research_questions: Do logged findings reach the grower sooner?

incremental.description: No ongoing upkeep: the grower sets up rows and plots, and learning the app is a one-off.

approvals.approved_version: The finding with row, symptom and photo exactly as checked by the worker in s4c, sent once to the grower in the crop registration app; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the grower is usually nearby, so findings are still told in person (0.8); high: the grower works elsewhere on a large site (3.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Ask about the customer's garden, recommend plants and care, check stock and prices, give care labels and answer later questions.

steps.what: Farmworker asks the customer about place, soil, light and wishes
Farmworker gives advice on plant selection and purchase and explains care
Farmworker walks to the office to check stock and prices
Farmworker writes care tips on a card for the customer
Farmworker answers follow-up questions by phone and e-mail

tasks.design: A tablet in the sales area shows stock and prices from the web shop on the {ECOMMERCE} platform, and care labels per variety print from the nursery's care text library, each with a code linking to a care page on the website in the {CMS}. The conversation and advice stay with the worker.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock lived in the office and care tips were handwritten each time.
tasks.enabler_now: Web shops show live stock, and label printers print from a text library.
tasks.still_hard: Good advice depends on knowing the plants and listening to the customer.
tasks.human_edge: Matching the right plant to someone's garden and habits.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes; more time for advice, less walking and writing.

reach.learn: Whether care pages cut repeat questions.

evidence.claim: Web shops show live stock on a tablet, and label printers print from a text library.
Chatbots that talk to the public must disclose they are AI; this design uses none.

assumptions: Boundary: from the customer's question to follow-up answers; the sale itself is outside.
Input contract: stock and prices kept by the grower in the web shop; care texts per variety written by the grower; fallback is the office and handwritten cards.
Grower time on care texts is upkeep.
unknowns: Number of retail customers per week.
How many varieties need care texts.
research_questions: Do care pages reduce follow-up calls?

incremental.description: Farmworker reports care texts that customers find unclear.
Grower writes and updates care texts per variety.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few retail visitors and many varieties without a care text, so cards are still written for many (9.7); high: care texts for most varieties (15.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The farmworker keeps scouting, treating, picking and advising; notes, spray records and delivery paperwork move to phone apps.
skills_to_grow: Logging findings and sprays in the field
Using live stock to advise customers
role.ambitious_version: A farmworker whose every finding and spray is recorded on the spot, ready for any inspection.

job.title: Farmworkers and Laborers, Crop, Nursery, and Greenhouse
